description: Combining warfarin and aspirin greatly increases bleeding risk. Avoid unless directed by a doctor.
NSAIDs like ibuprofen increase bleeding risk when taken with warfarin.
Naproxen can displace warfarin from proteins, increasing anticoagulant effect.
Alcohol with metformin increases risk of lactic acidosis, a dangerous condition.
Grapefruit juice inhibits enzymes that break down simvastatin, causing toxic buildup.
Grapefruit juice raises atorvastatin levels in the blood significantly.
ACE inhibitors like lisinopril raise potassium; extra potassium supplements can be dangerous.
High potassium foods like bananas can interact mildly with ACE inhibitors.
Many salt substitutes contain potassium chloride, which may cause hyperkalemia with ACE inhibitors.
Dairy calcium can reduce ciprofloxacin absorption. Take 2 hours before or after dairy.
Antacids with calcium or magnesium reduce ciprofloxacin absorption.
Coffee can reduce levothyroxine absorption. Take thyroid medication 30-60 minutes before coffee.
Calcium can bind to levothyroxine and reduce absorption. Space doses 4 hours apart.
Antacids reduce levothyroxine absorption. Space doses by at least 4 hours.
Alcohol increases risk of liver damage when combined with methotrexate. Avoid alcohol completely.
NSAIDs like ibuprofen reduce methotrexate excretion, causing toxic levels.
Combining SSRIs with tramadol can cause serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition.
Combining SSRIs with MAOIs can cause fatal serotonin syndrome. Never take together.
St. John's Wort increases serotonin and combined with fluoxetine can cause serotonin syndrome.
Alcohol can increase sedative effects and worsen depression when taken with sertraline.
Alcohol does not significantly interact with amoxicillin but may worsen side effects like nausea.
Calcium in dairy products binds to tetracycline and prevents absorption. Avoid dairy near dose time.
Iron binds to tetracycline and reduces its absorption and effectiveness.
High fiber foods (bran, oats) can reduce digoxin absorption. Maintain consistent diet.
Licorice can lower potassium levels, increasing digoxin toxicity risk.
Foods high in tyramine (aged cheese, red wine, cured meats) with MAOIs can cause dangerous blood pressure spikes.
Red wine contains tyramine which can cause hypertensive crisis with MAOI antidepressants.
Aged cheeses are high in tyramine which interacts fatally with MAOIs.
Omeprazole reduces the effectiveness of clopidogrel by inhibiting its activation enzyme.
Regular alcohol use with statins increases risk of liver damage.
Combining metronidazole with alcohol causes severe nausea, vomiting, and flushing (disulfiram-like reaction).
Like metronidazole, tinidazole causes severe reactions with alcohol. Avoid for 3 days after last dose.
Grapefruit juice increases amlodipine blood levels, potentially causing low blood pressure.
Grapefruit juice significantly increases buspirone levels, increasing side effects.
One of the most sensitive drugs to grapefruit juice interaction. Blood levels can triple.
Grapefruit juice dramatically increases cyclosporine levels, causing toxicity.
Grapefruit juice markedly increases tacrolimus blood levels.
Foods high in vitamin K (kale, spinach, broccoli) reduce warfarin effectiveness. Keep intake consistent.
Cranberry juice may increase warfarin effect and raise bleeding risk.
Occasional alcohol may slightly increase warfarin effect; heavy use unpredictably alters INR.
Combining sildenafil (Viagra) with nitrates can cause a dangerous and potentially fatal drop in blood pressure.
Both are CNS depressants. Combined they can cause extreme sedation, respiratory depression, or death.
Combining opioids with alcohol severely increases risk of respiratory depression and death.
This combination is responsible for many overdose deaths. Both suppress breathing.
NSAIDs raise lithium levels in the blood, causing toxicity.
High caffeine intake followed by sudden reduction can raise lithium levels.
High sodium diets lower lithium levels; low sodium raises them. Maintain consistent salt intake.
Antacids significantly reduce doxycycline absorption. Space doses by at least 2 hours.
Dairy reduces doxycycline absorption though less so than with tetracycline.
Alcohol can both increase and decrease phenytoin levels unpredictably, increasing seizure risk.
Grapefruit has minor interaction with phenytoin; still worth monitoring.
Grapefruit juice significantly increases carbamazepine levels, raising toxicity risk.
Alcohol may reduce seizure threshold and interact with carbamazepine metabolism.
Alcohol increases risk of stomach bleeding when combined with ibuprofen.
Alcohol combined with aspirin increases stomach bleeding risk.
Spironolactone retains potassium; adding potassium supplements can cause dangerous hyperkalemia.
Potassium-based salt substitutes can cause dangerous potassium buildup with spironolactone.
Alcohol with prednisone increases risk of stomach ulcers and immune suppression.
NSAIDs combined with corticosteroids greatly increase risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
Antacids reduce the absorption of ketoconazole by reducing stomach acid needed for dissolution.
Rifampin reduces the effectiveness of birth control pills by speeding up their metabolism.
